conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the evidence indicates masks worn by a large proportion of the population can reduce COVID-19 infections, citing multiple supporting studies. Therefore, it endorses the claim.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
# Evidence on Population-Wide Masking and COVID-19 Infections

**Conclusion: The evidence indicates the answer is yes—not no. Masks worn by a large proportion of the population can reduce COVID-19 infections.**

Multiple studies support this finding:

- A **systematic literature review** (MDPI, 2025) concluded that "masking policies and mask wearing are beneficial to prevent and reduce the risk of SARS-CoV-2 infections and COVID-19 disease in various real-world settings." ([MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590))

- A **PNAS study** using survey data from 20 million people across six continents found that "population mask wearing notably reduced SARS-CoV-2 transmission (mean mask-wearing levels corresponding to a 19% decrease in R)." ([PNAS](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119))

- A **meta-analysis** (Springer, 2025) reported that "after controlling for publication bias, wearing a face mask is associated with a reduced risk of COVID-19 infection by 11.8% to 28.5%." ([Springer](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s41885-025-00185-5.pdf))

- A large-scale **community trial** (discussed in The Conversation) found COVID-19 fell by 35% for people aged 60+ and 23% for those 50–60, with surgical and cloth masks yielding a 12% reduction in COVID-19-like symptoms. ([The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/evidence-shows-that-yes-masks-prevent-covid-19-and-surgical-masks-are-the-way-to-go-167963))

While effect sizes vary by mask type, setting, and population, the overall body of evidence consistently supports that population-level mask wearing reduces SARS-CoV-2 transmission and infection rates.
